chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.section: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.text:
## Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
Published/updated: 2026-11-12
Moving out is stressful enough without worrying about whether you’ll get your security deposit back. You’re packing boxes, coordinating movers, forwarding mail, and somewhere in the middle of all that, you’re supposed to deep clean an entire apartment or house to a standard that satisfies your landlord.
Here’s the thing most renters find out too late: landlords and property managers in Minnesota have specific expectations when you hand over the keys. These aren’t always written in plain language in your lease. Miss a few spots, and you could lose hundreds of dollars from your deposit, even if you’ve been a model tenant for years.
This checklist covers exactly what landlords expect, what renters tend to forget, and how to handle the whole process without losing your mind or your money. If you decide you’d rather hand this off to professionals, our covers every item on this list. move-in/move-out cleaning service

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.section: Why Move-Out Cleaning Matters More Than You Think
chunks.text:
## Why Move-Out Cleaning Matters More Than You Think
Minnesota law gives landlords three weeks after you vacate to return your deposit or send an itemized list of deductions. Cleaning costs are one of the most common deductions landlords make, and they’re also among the easiest to dispute if you have documentation.
A thorough clean before you leave protects your money. It also protects your rental history, since some landlords report cleaning disputes to tenant screening services.
The flip side is true for landlords too. A property that’s clean and ready to show can be re-rented faster, which means less vacancy loss. For property managers handling multiple units, having a consistent cleaning standard makes turnover smoother.
Both sides benefit when the move-out clean is done right. The problem is they often have different ideas of what “right” looks like.

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.section: What Most Leases Actually Say About Cleaning
chunks.text:
## What Most Leases Actually Say About Cleaning
Most residential leases in Minnesota include language requiring tenants to return the property in the same condition as when they moved in, minus normal wear and tear. That phrase, “normal wear and tear,” does a lot of heavy lifting.
Scuffs on baseboards from furniture? Normal wear and tear. A grease-coated stovetop that hasn’t been cleaned in two years? Not normal wear and tear.
Faded paint from sunlight? Normal. Crayon on the wall? Not normal.
Dust on ceiling fans? Landlords vary on this one. Pet hair embedded in carpet? That’s a charge.
The safest approach is to treat the property as if it were a hotel room on checkout day. If something looks like it needs attention, it probably does.
## The Complete Move-Out Cleaning Checklist
Work through this room by room. Check each item as you go, and take photos when you’re done. Those photos are your evidence if any deposit dispute comes up later.

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.text:
## Kitchen
The kitchen is where most deposit deductions happen. Landlords know that kitchens get heavy use, and they look carefully.
- Clean inside and outside of all cabinets and drawers
- Wipe down cabinet doors and handles
- Clean the stovetop, including burners, grates, and drip pans
- Degrease the range hood and filter
- Clean inside the oven, including the oven door glass
- Wipe down the refrigerator inside and outside, including the rubber door seal
- Clean the freezer and defrost if needed
- Wipe down the microwave inside and outside
- Clean the dishwasher interior, filter, and door seal
- Scrub the sink and polish the faucet
- Clean the garbage disposal (ice cubes and salt work well)
- Wipe down all countertops
- Sweep and mop the floor, including under the refrigerator
- Clean light fixtures and replace any burned-out bulbs
A note on the refrigerator: it needs to be running and set to a normal temperature when you leave. If you defrost the freezer, dry it completely before you’re done.

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.text:
## Bathrooms
Bathrooms require attention to detail. Soap scum, mold around the tub, and mineral buildup on faucets are the most common issues.
- Scrub the toilet bowl, seat, tank, and base
- Clean the bathtub or shower, including grout lines
- Remove soap scum from shower doors or curtain liner
- Check for and clean any mold or mildew (especially in corners and around the caulk)
- Clean the sink and polish the faucet
- Wipe down the vanity and mirror
- Clean inside and outside of cabinets and medicine cabinet
- Mop the floor, including behind the toilet
- Empty and clean the exhaust fan cover
- Replace any missing or broken towel hooks or toilet paper holders (or report them)
If there’s mold in the bathroom, clean it with an appropriate solution. Document it before you clean it if it was there when you moved in.

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.text:
## Bedrooms
Bedrooms are simpler, but they still require a complete pass.
- Vacuum the carpet or mop hardwood floors
- Move furniture out before vacuuming to get corners and edges
- Wipe down baseboards
- Clean windowsills and window tracks
- Wipe down closet shelves and rods
- Clean light fixtures and ceiling fan blades
- Patch small nail holes with spackle (or notify your landlord of larger holes)
- Wipe down door frames and light switches
If you have carpet, consider whether it needs a professional steam clean. Some leases require it regardless of condition. Check yours.
## Living and Common Areas
- Vacuum or mop all floors
- Wipe down baseboards throughout
- Clean windowsills, windows (inside), and window tracks
- Wipe down light switches and outlet covers
- Clean ceiling fans
- Dust light fixtures
- Wipe down any built-in shelving
- Clean the front door and any sliding doors, including tracks
- Sweep the entryway
## Walls and Ceilings
This is where renters often get caught. Landlords look at walls closely because paint and drywall repairs are expensive.
- Spot-clean any marks or scuffs you can remove
- Report any damage you can’t clean up, rather than hoping they won’t notice
- Check for cobwebs in ceiling corners
- Wipe down air vents and return registers

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.text:
## Laundry Area (if Applicable)
- Clean the washer drum and door seal
- Wipe down the exterior of washer and dryer
- Clean the lint trap and the area behind the dryer
- Sweep or mop the floor
## Garage, Patio, or Storage Areas
- Remove all personal belongings
- Sweep the garage floor
- Clean up any oil stains if possible
- Empty and clean any storage areas that were included in your lease
## What Renters Forget Most Often
After years of experience with move-out cleans across,,, and other Minnesota communities, these are the spots that get missed most often: Eden Prairie Minnetonka Plymouth
Inside kitchen cabinets. People wipe the fronts but forget the shelves inside. Landlords check.
The oven. Specifically the oven door glass and the area under the bottom burner panel. This takes time and the right cleaner.
Window tracks. Easy to overlook, often full of dead bugs and debris.
The refrigerator coils or the area beneath the refrigerator. Moving it out to clean underneath is worth the effort.
Behind and under appliances. Food debris and grease build up in places you haven’t looked since you moved in.
Ceiling fan blades. Dust accumulates on top of the blades where it’s not visible from below.
The bathroom exhaust fan cover. It collects dust and is almost never cleaned during regular tidying.

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.section: Should You Hire a Professional Move-Out Cleaning Service?
chunks.text:
## Should You Hire a Professional Move-Out Cleaning Service?
For some people, doing it yourself makes sense. For others, the calculation tips the other way pretty quickly.
Consider what your time is worth on moving day. If you’re packing, supervising movers, doing a walkthrough, and managing a dozen other tasks, adding a thorough clean of an entire home to that list is genuinely difficult. Rushing through it increases the risk of missing things and losing deposit money.
A professional move-out cleaning service covers every item on this list systematically. The cleaners know what landlords look for because they’ve done this hundreds of times. They bring the right equipment for things like oven cleaning, grout scrubbing, and window tracks.
In many cases, the cost of a professional clean is less than what a landlord would deduct for an incomplete job.
Our works throughout,,,,, and surrounding communities. We can schedule your clean around your move-out timeline. move-in/move-out cleaning team Minneapolis Edina Maple Grove Wayzata Excelsior

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.text:
## For Landlords and Property Managers
If you manage rental properties, having a written cleaning standard you give to tenants at the start of the lease removes ambiguity at move-out. Include the specific expectations for the kitchen, bathrooms, and carpets, and whether professional carpet cleaning is required.
A move-in inspection report with photos sets the baseline. A move-out report with the same photos makes any deductions easy to document and defend.
Many property managers in the Twin Cities area schedule a professional move out cleaning between every tenant. It’s a reliable way to maintain consistent property condition and shortens the time a unit sits vacant. If you’re managing multiple units, our options might work well for your schedule. recurring cleaning

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.section: Cleaning vs. Damage: Knowing the Difference
chunks.text:
## Cleaning vs. Damage: Knowing the Difference
This is worth understanding clearly before you hand over the keys.
Landlords can charge for cleaning that returns the property to its move-in condition. They cannot charge for normal wear and tear, which includes things like small nail holes, minor carpet wear in high-traffic areas, and faded paint.
If a landlord attempts to charge you for something that falls under normal wear and tear, you can dispute it. Minnesota’s tenant protection statutes are reasonably clear on this. The provides guidance on security deposit disputes if you run into problems. Minnesota Attorney General’s office
Document everything with photos and keep a copy of your move-in inspection report.
## How to Handle the Final Walkthrough
Request a walkthrough with your landlord or property manager before you leave. This gives you a chance to address anything they point out on the spot rather than receive a deduction letter three weeks later.
If they note something during the walkthrough, you have an opportunity to clean it before the keys are officially handed over. Some landlords will do this, some won’t. It’s worth asking.
Bring your completed checklist and your photos to the walkthrough. They show you took the process seriously.
Wondering what your landlord will actually check? Read. what landlords inspect during move-out

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.text:
## Frequently Asked Questions
Do I have to professionally clean the carpets when I move out?
It depends on your lease. Some Minnesota leases require professional carpet cleaning regardless of condition. If yours doesn’t specify, and the carpet is in the same condition as when you moved in (accounting for normal wear), you likely aren’t required to pay for professional cleaning. Check your lease language carefully.
How long does a move-out clean take?
For a solo renter doing it personally, a one-bedroom apartment takes three to five hours if done thoroughly. A larger home can take a full day. Professional move-out cleaners typically work faster because they work in teams and bring efficient equipment.
Can my landlord charge me if the apartment isn’t perfectly clean?
Yes, if the property requires cleaning beyond what’s attributable to normal use, a landlord can deduct reasonable cleaning costs from your deposit. The key word is “reasonable.” They can’t charge you $500 to clean a single-bedroom apartment.
What if there was mold when I moved in?
If you documented mold at move-in (noted on your move-in checklist or reported in writing to the landlord), you should not be charged for it at move-out. This is why a thorough move-in inspection matters.
What’s the difference between a standard clean and a move-out clean?

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.text:
## Frequently Asked Questions (cont.)
A standard clean maintains a property that’s already in good shape. A move-out clean is more thorough, covering areas that typically aren’t touched during regular cleaning: inside appliances, inside cabinets, window tracks, baseboards, and behind appliances.
How soon before my move-out date should I schedule professional cleaning?
Schedule your clean for the day before or the morning of your move-out, after your belongings are out. Cleaning before the furniture is gone leaves too many missed spots.
Is move-out cleaning included in regular maid service?
No. Move-out cleaning is a separate, more detailed service. Regular cleaning maintains a home that’s already tidy. Move-out cleaning addresses years of accumulated buildup in areas that don’t get touched during routine cleaning.
How often do landlords have to cleanup when tenants move out?
Landlords generally need to clean a rental property, before the next tenant moves in. This helps keep the property clean, presentable, and ready for the next occupant. every time a tenant moves out

chunks.title: Blog: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist: What Renters and Landlords Both Expect in Minnesota
chunks.section: Ready to Take This Off Your Plate?

## Cleaning for Mental Health: Boost Well Being with a Tidy Space
Published/updated: 2026-02-25
Ever feel calmer after tidying up your space? Turns out, cleanliness isn’t just about looks it has a big impact on mental health too. A neat environment can reduce stress, ease anxiety, and help you focus better. In this blog, we’ll explore how cleanliness affects your mind, the benefits of an organized space, and simple tips to help you start cleaning today!
## The Link Between Cleanliness and Mental Health
Research has shown that there is a strong link between cleanliness and mental health. A cluttered environment can lead to feelings of overwhelm and anxiety. When your surroundings are messy, it can be challenging to concentrate, leading to decreased productivity and increased stress levels. On the other hand, a clean house can create a sense of calm and control, which is essential for maintaining good mental health.
## The Psychological Impact of Clutter
- Increased Stress: Clutter can be a constant reminder of unfinished tasks, leading to heightened stress levels.
- Decreased Focus: A messy environment can distract you, making it hard to concentrate on important tasks.
- Feelings of Overwhelm: The sight of disorganization can make you feel overwhelmed, leading to procrastination.

## Benefits of Cleaning for Mental Health
Cleaning and mental health are closely intertwined. Here are some benefits of maintaining a clean space:
- Improved Mood: A tidy environment can boost your mood and create a sense of accomplishment.
- Enhanced Productivity: A clean house allows for better focus, leading to increased productivity.
- Reduced Anxiety: A clutter-free space can help reduce feelings of anxiety and promote relaxation.
- Better Sleep: A clean bedroom can lead to improved sleep quality, which is vital for mental health.
- Increased Motivation: A clean space can inspire you to take on new challenges and projects.
## Practical Tips for Cleaning Your Space
Want to feel calmer, more focused, and in control? Cleaning can be a simple but powerful way to boost your mood. Here are some easy tips to help you get started small steps that make a big difference! chunks.title: Blog: Cleaning for Mental Health: Boost Well Being with a Tidy Space
chunks.text:
## Start Small
- Focus on One Room: Begin with one room or area to avoid feeling overwhelmed.
- Set a Timer: Dedicate a specific amount of time to cleaning, such as 15 or 30 minutes.
## Declutter Regularly
- Sort Items: Go through your belongings and decide what to keep, donate, or throw away.
- Use the “One In, One Out” Rule: For every new item you bring into your home, consider removing one.
## Create a Cleaning Schedule
- Daily Tasks: Make a list of daily cleaning tasks, such as making your bed or washing dishes.
- Weekly Deep Cleaning: Set aside time each week for deeper cleaning tasks, like vacuuming or dusting.
## Involve Others
- Family Participation: Encourage family members to help with cleaning tasks to make it a shared responsibility.
- Friends’ Cleaning Day: Invite friends over for a cleaning day, turning a chore into a fun social activity.

From steam-cleaning your microwave with lemon water to refreshing your coffee maker with a vinegar brew cycle, these quick, natural techniques make deep cleaning feel effortless. Even your refrigerator coils and dishwasher deserve a little love to boost efficiency and extend their lifespan. And to make it all even easier, Shinenos is offering this Labor Day weekend—because every hardworking tool deserves a fresh start. 10% off all cleaning

chunks.title: Blog: Labor Day Cleaning: Give Your Kitchen Heroes a Quick Refresh
chunks.text:
## Tackle appliances with time-saving techniques
Your kitchen appliances work hard all year long, and Labor Day weekend offers the perfect opportunity to give them some much-needed attention. Start with your microwave by placing a bowl of water with lemon slices inside and running it for two minutes. The steam loosens stuck-on food while the lemon naturally deodorizes. Simply wipe down the interior with a damp cloth afterward.
For your oven, create a paste using baking soda and water, spread it on stubborn spots, and let it sit while you tackle other tasks. The dishwasher benefits from a simple cleaning cycle using white vinegar – just place a bowl of vinegar on the top rack and run a hot cycle. Your refrigerator coils deserve attention too; vacuum them to improve energy efficiency and extend your appliance’s lifespan.
Coffee makers and small appliances often get overlooked but respond well to a vinegar solution. Run a brew cycle with equal parts water and white vinegar, followed by two cycles of plain water to rinse. For blenders and food processors, fill them halfway with warm water, add a drop of dish soap, and run for 30 seconds before rinsing.
: Make your appliance cleaning even easier with Shinenos products – enjoy 10% off all cleaning this Labor Day weekend! Special Labor Day Offer [ CLAIM YOUR 10% OFF HERE]

chunks.title: Blog: Labor Day Cleaning: Give Your Kitchen Heroes a Quick Refresh
chunks.text:
## Sanitize countertops and backsplashes efficiently
Different countertop materials require specific care approaches for optimal results. Granite and natural stone surfaces need pH-neutral cleaners to avoid etching, while laminate counters can handle most general-purpose cleaners. Create an all-purpose solution using warm water, dish soap, and a splash of white vinegar for most surfaces.
Your backsplash collects grease and food splatters daily, making it a priority area for your labor day house cleaning checklist. For tile backsplashes, focus extra attention on grout lines using an old toothbrush and a paste made from baking soda and water. Glass backsplashes shine beautifully with a mixture of water and rubbing alcohol in a spray bottle.
Start from top to bottom when cleaning these surfaces. Spray your chosen cleaner and let it sit for a few minutes to break down grease and grime. Use microfiber cloths for streak-free results, and always have multiple cloths ready – one for cleaning and another for drying.
For stubborn stains, make a paste using baking soda and just enough water to bind it together. Apply this paste to problem areas, let it work for 10 minutes, then scrub gently with a soft brush or cloth. This method works particularly well on coffee stains and water spots.

chunks.title: Blog: Labor Day Cleaning: Give Your Kitchen Heroes a Quick Refresh
chunks.text:
## Organize pantry and refrigerator contents
Smart organization transforms your kitchen’s functionality and makes meal preparation significantly easier. Begin with your refrigerator by removing everything and checking expiration dates. Group similar items together – dairy products in one area, leftovers in another, and condiments organized by frequency of use.
Invest in clear storage containers for your pantry items. Transfer cereals, pasta, rice, and other dry goods into airtight containers that stack neatly. Label everything with contents and expiration dates using a label maker or masking tape and marker. This system prevents food waste and makes inventory management simple.
Create zones in your pantry based on meal types and cooking frequency. Keep breakfast items at eye level, lunch nearby, and dinner ingredients grouped logically. Store heavy items like canned goods on lower shelves for safety and accessibility.
Your spice collection deserves special attention during this deep clean. Check expiration dates – ground spices lose potency after two years, while whole spices last longer. Arrange spices alphabetically or by cuisine type, whichever system works better for your cooking style. Consider using a spice rack or drawer organizer to maximize space and visibility.

chunks.title: Blog: Labor Day Cleaning: Give Your Kitchen Heroes a Quick Refresh
chunks.text:
## Organize pantry and refrigerator contents (cont.)
The refrigerator’s crisper drawers often become forgotten zones where vegetables turn into science experiments. Clean these drawers thoroughly and line them with paper towels to absorb excess moisture. Store fruits and vegetables in their optimal locations – some produce needs high humidity while others prefer it dry.

## How to Organize Your Home Like a Minimalist
Published/updated: 2026-02-24
Have you ever felt like your home still looks messy even after you’ve cleaned it? You’re not alone.
Sometimes, the problem isn’t dirt it’s clutter. Too many things, too many colors, too much going on. That’s where the minimalist lifestyle comes in. It’s not about having an empty house or owning nothing. It’s about creating space for what truly matters calm, function, and balance.
And the best part? A minimalist home isn’t just beautiful it’s easier to clean and maintain. Let’s explore how you can organize your home like a minimalist and create a space that feels calm, airy, and stress-free.

chunks.title: Blog: How to Organize Your Home Like a Minimalist
chunks.text:
## 1. Declutter with Purpose
Minimalism isn’t about living with nothing it’s about living with intention. The first and most important step in creating a minimalist home is decluttering, but not just any kind of decluttering. You’re not simply throwing things away; you’re making mindful choices about what truly deserves a place in your home and in your life.
Before you start organizing or decorating, take time to go through your belongings one by one. Ask yourself two simple but powerful questions:
“Do I use this regularly?”
If something has been sitting untouched for months, there’s a good chance you don’t actually need it. A practical rule to follow is the 90/90 rule if you haven’t used an item in the last 90 days and don’t plan to use it in the next 90, it’s probably time to let it go. Be honest with yourself. Many of us keep things out of guilt (“I spent money on it”) or fear (“I might need it someday”), but the truth is that most of those “somedays” never come.
“Does it make my life easier or bring me joy?”

chunks.title: Blog: How to Organize Your Home Like a Minimalist
chunks.text:
## 1. Declutter with Purpose (cont.)
Minimalism doesn’t mean stripping your home of personality or comfort. Some items might not be used daily but still hold emotional or practical value like your favorite coffee mug, a cozy blanket, or a framed photo that reminds you of a happy memory. These things deserve to stay because they contribute to your happiness and well-being. The goal isn’t to have less; it’s to have only what matters most.
Start small and stay consistent. Trying to declutter an entire house in a single day can feel overwhelming. Instead, focus on one drawer, one shelf, or one corner at a time. It’s not about speed it’s about making thoughtful decisions. Even 15 minutes a day can make a visible difference within a week.
As you sort through your items, divide everything into three categories:
- Keep: Things you use regularly or truly love. These are your essentials the items that add convenience or joy to your everyday life.
- Donate/Sell: Items that are still in good condition but no longer serve you. Let someone else enjoy them instead of letting them collect dust in storage. Donating not only frees your space but can also make a positive impact on someone else’s life.
- Toss: Broken, expired, or unusable items. It’s okay to let go of things that have served their purpose. Holding onto clutter only creates more stress and less space.

chunks.title: Blog: How to Organize Your Home Like a Minimalist
chunks.text:
## 1. Declutter with Purpose (cont.)
Remember, minimalism isn’t about getting rid of everything or living in a bare, empty space. It’s about keeping only what adds real value items that serve a purpose, bring comfort, or reflect who you truly are. Every object in your home should earn its place.
When you declutter with intention, you’ll notice how your space starts to breathe again. You’ll move easier, clean faster, and feel lighter mentally. A clear home often leads to a clear mind and that’s where the beauty of minimalism truly begins.

## 2. Simplify Your Space
Once you’ve decluttered, it’s time to simplify the look and feel of your rooms.
A minimalist home emphasizes functionality and balance. Every item has a purpose and a place.
Here are a few simple ways to get started:
- Choose neutral colors like white, beige, or light gray to create a calm, open feeling.2.
- Pick multifunctional furniture (like storage benches or nesting tables).
- Hide the clutter using baskets, bins, or cabinets with clean lines.
- Let natural light fill your space it instantly makes a room feel fresh.
You don’t need to redesign your home overnight. Start by simplifying one area maybe your living room or workspace.

chunks.title: Blog: How to Organize Your Home Like a Minimalist
chunks.section: 3. Build a Routine You Can Stick To
chunks.text:
## 3. Build a Routine You Can Stick To
A minimalist home isn’t built in a weekend, it’s maintained through simple habits.
Think of cleaning and organizing as part of your lifestyle, not a chore. Here are a few easy routines that make a big difference:
- 5-minute tidy-up: Before bed, put away anything out of place.
- Wipe surfaces daily: Keeps dust and crumbs from piling up.
- Weekly reset: Vacuum, change linens, clean bathrooms.
- One-in, one-out rule: Every time you buy something new, remove one old item.
These small actions prevent clutter from building up again and keep your home feeling calm and fresh
## 4. Let Go of Perfection
One of the biggest misconceptions about minimalism is that your home has to look like a magazine. It doesn’t.
It’s okay if your kids’ toys are out or if the coffee table isn’t styled perfectly. What matters is that your home feels peaceful, functional, and welcoming. A minimalist home isn’t about perfection it’s about intention.
When you stop chasing perfection and start embracing simplicity, you’ll find it’s much easier to keep things clean both physically and mentally.

chunks.title: Blog: How to Organize Your Home Like a Minimalist
chunks.text:
## 5.Maintaining a Minimalist Home with Ease
Once your home is simplified, keeping it that way becomes much easier as long as you maintain a few gentle habits.
Try making checklist that keeps your space consistently tidy: a monthly cleaning
- Vacuum and mop all floors
- Wipe down all flat surfaces
- Clean windows and mirrors
- Refresh bedding and towels
- Deep clean kitchen and bathrooms
Doing a little bit regularly is always easier than doing a lot all at once.
## Clean Home, Clear Mind
Minimalism isn’t about less, it’s about more of what matters. More space. More peace. More time.
When you organize your home like a minimalist, you’re not just creating a cleaner space you’re creating a calmer lifestyle. And with the right cleaning routine (or ), you can keep that sense of calm every day. Keeping your home clean, simple, and stress free, so you can focus on living beautifully. a little help from Shinenos
